extracted.intended_audience: researchers of science communication, press officers at medical universities, health journalists, and policy-makers interested in media representation of medical research
extracted.subtask_description: Content-analysis–style evaluation of medical-university press releases (PRs) and their corresponding news stories (NSs), using predefined scientific and interest-raising measures and a 0–12 quality score. The study establishes which items are reported or omitted, how exaggeration is measured, and how PR presence influences NS presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct reporting of the main aim of the scientific paper in the PR and/or NS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as one of the quality measures. In the sample, present in 74% of PRs and 32% of NSs. Used in calculation of mean percentage of presence in NSs and PR influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct reporting of the study design of the scientific paper in the PR and/or NS (e.g., randomized trial, cohort, cross-sectional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deemed an essential quality measure. Present in 84% of PRs and 63% of NSs. Presence in PRs increased probability of presence in NSs (Mean PR Influence Factor reported).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent variable (IV) reported in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the independent variable (exposure) is correctly mentioned in the PR and/or NS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in quality measures. Present in 96% of PRs and 82% of NSs. Also considered whether IV appears in the title (see separate metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent variable (DV) reported in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the dependent variable (outcome) is correctly mentioned in the PR and/or NS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in quality measures. Present in 92% of PRs and 84% of NSs. Note: when DV was absent in PRs NSs sometimes still reported it (DV reporting in NSs 92% when absent in PRs in one comparison).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship IV–DV in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the relationship between IV and DV (how they relate) is stated correctly in the PR and/or NS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of quality measures. Present in 48% of PRs and 54% of NSs. The study also analyses exaggeration of this relationship (see Exaggeration criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the sample size of the study is reported in the PR and/or NS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the 12 quality measures. Present in 64% of PRs and 62% of NSs. Presence in PRs markedly increased chance of presence in NSs (Mean PR Influence Factor 2.1, p<0.001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Main results
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting of the study's main results (qualitative/summary) in the PR and/or NS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among quality measures. Reported in 100% of PRs and 98% of NSs in this sample. Treated as essential; used in scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether results are quantified (e.g., effect sizes, percentages, absolute risks) rather than only described qualitatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential quality measure. Present in 60% of PRs and 55% of NSs. Had the highest Mean PR Influence Factor (14.1, p<0.001): when present in PRs, much more likely to appear quantified in NSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the main conclusions of the scientific paper are correctly reported in the PR and/or NS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the 12 quality measures. Present in 92% of PRs and 96% of NSs. Presence in PRs increases likelihood of presence in NSs (Mean PR Influence Factor 1.2, p=0.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Most important limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the principal limitations of the scientific study are reported in the PR and/or NS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential quality measure but frequently omitted: present in 21% of both PRs and NSs. Presence in PRs strongly increased chance of presence in NSs (Mean PR Influence Factor 4.3, p<0.001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the source(s) of funding for the research are reported in the PR and/or NS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential quality measure. Present in 59% of PRs but only 7% of NSs. Presence in PRs modestly increased reporting in NSs (Mean PR Influence Factor reported; p values noted in tables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether potential conflicts of interest declared in the scientific paper are reported in the PR and/or NS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential quality measure. Present in 16% of relevant PRs and 3% of relevant NSs (analysed in subgroup of SPs declaring potential conflicts). Presence in PRs associated with higher reporting in NSs (Mean PR Influence Factor ~5.7, p=0.08).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship IV–DV in title
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the PR/NS title states the relationship between IV and DV (e.g., headline implying association or causation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the additional scientific measures. Present in 35% of PRs and 29% of NSs. Presence in PRs increased probability of presence in NSs (Mean PR Influence Factor 1.7, p=0.004).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent variable (IV) in title
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the IV appears in the PR/NS title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific measure included. IV in title present in 85% of PRs and 66% of NSs. Presence in PRs increased presence in NS titles (Mean PR Influence Factor 1.5, p=0.003).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent variable (DV) in title
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the DV appears in the PR/NS title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific measure included. DV in title present in 84% of PRs and 59% of NSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control group
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the study's control group (if applicable) is reported in the PR and/or NS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among scientific measures. Present in 65% of PRs and 36% of NSs. Presence in PRs had a large PR Influence Factor (6.1, p<0.001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Base rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether baseline risk or base rate information is reported in the PR and/or NS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific measure. Present in 32% of PRs and 36% of NSs. Presence in PRs increased NS reporting (Mean PR Influence Factor 3.2, p<0.001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exaggeration of IV–DV
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the PR and/or NS makes a stronger claim about the relationship between IV and DV than the SP (e.g., SP reports correlation but PR/NS implies causation or uses 'can').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured in a subgroup of SPs that did not report causal statements. Exaggeration occurred in 34% of PRs and 60% of NSs. NSs were significantly more likely to exaggerate when PRs exaggerated (Mean PR Influence Factor 1.53, p=0.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Seven-category relationship statement taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of the stated IV–DV relationship into seven categories: no statement about relationship, statement of no relationship, statement of correlation, ambiguous statement of relationship, conditional statement of relationship, statement of 'can', and statement of causation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to standardize how strength of inference is coded across SP, PR, NS. Mirrors Sumner et al.'s approach and is central to identifying exaggeration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality score (0–12) based on 12 essential measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate score counting how many of the 12 essential scientific measures are correctly reported in a PR or NS (range 0–12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twelve measures: main aim, study design, IV, DV, relationship IV–DV, sample size, main results, quantification of results, main conclusion, most important limitations, funding, conflict of interest. PR mean = 8.0 (SD 1.5), NS mean = 6.5 (SD 1.7). Used for comparative tests (Wilcoxon signed-rank) and correlation (Spearman).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mean PR Influence Factor
rubrics_metrics.description: A metric calculated per measure as the ratio of mean percentage of presence in NSs when the measure was present in the PR to the mean percentage of presence in NSs when the measure was absent in the PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to quantify how presence of a measure in a PR influences its uptake in NSs. Reported per measure (e.g., quantification 14.1, control group 6.1, 'first' 4.7). Statistical significance tested with t-tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether quotes (e.g., from researchers) appear in PRs and/or NSs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified as an interest-raising measure. Present in 99% of PRs and 90% of NSs. Presence had small PR Influence Factor for NSs in this sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground‑breaking words in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Use in the text of words such as 'ground-breaking', 'breakthrough', or similar interest-raising wording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest-raising measure. Present in 7% of PRs and 11% of NSs. Also separately coded when present inside quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground‑breaking words in quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of ground‑breaking or hyperbolic language inside quoted material in PRs/NSs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest-raising sub-item. Present in 8% of PRs and 8% of NSs in the sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice in quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the PR/NS includes advice directed at readers inside quoted material (e.g., 'you should...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest-raising measure. Present in 35% of PRs and 14% of NSs. Presence in PRs strongly increased chance of inclusion in NSs (Mean PR Influence Factor 2.9, p<0.001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the word 'first'
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the PR/NS uses the word 'first' to describe findings (an interest-raising practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest-raising measure. Present in 44% of PRs and 19% of NSs. Presence in PRs strongly increased NS uptake (Mean PR Influence Factor 4.7, p<0.001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the word 'new'
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the PR/NS uses the word 'new' at least once (interest-raising).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest-raising measure. Present in 77% of PRs and 55% of NSs. Presence in PRs increased NS probability (Mean PR Influence Factor 1.6, p=0.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjective words in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of subjective or evaluative wording in text (interest-raising wording beyond factual description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest-raising measure. Present in 41% of PRs and 51% of NSs. NSs showed more subjective wording than PRs (p=0.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct reporting relative to the scientific paper (SP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether PR/NS reports correspond correctly to the content and claims of the original scientific paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coders compared PRs to SPs and NSs to PRs using codebooks. For NS coding, coders were blinded to SP to simulate journalistic practice. Differences between SP and PR/NS (e.g., exaggerations) were explicitly recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coder blinding for NS coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Coding protocol where coders using the NS-vs-PR codebook were blinded to the original scientific paper to simulate journalistic interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of evaluation methodology to approximate how journalists would interpret PRs. Blinding affects how 'correct' reporting is judged for NSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater reliability & double-coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol to establish coding reliability: 25% of PRs and NSs were randomly selected for double-coding and analysed using kappa statistics and percentage agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall kappa reported as 0.53 with percent agreement 0.85, indicating moderate agreement. Used to assess and report coder reliability; coders resolved uncertainties by discussion when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion criteria for PRs and NSs
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural criteria for which PRs/NSs to include in analysis: PRs must be medical and directly related to a published scientific paper in a recognized journal; NSs included if they discussed the SP; opinion pieces and pieces written by the authors were excluded; max 12 NSs per PR; language and date-window selection applied per country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These selection rules determine the study sample and hence what PR/NS characteristics the rubric applies to. Search windows were three days before PR until two weeks after; databases included LexisNexis, Retriever, and Google News.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on news stories per press release
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum of 12 news stories per PR included in analysis to avoid oversampling viral cascades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than 12 NSs existed, priority was given to highest-ranked articles in the databases; reprints of press agency copy were collapsed to the original agency article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: contextualize findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical guidance that PRs should contextualize findings as much as possible (e.g., state limitations, funding, conflicts) to improve public understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on study conclusions: reporting caveats improves credibility and does not reduce uptake; PRs are part of branding but should include study limitations, funding, and COIs to avoid misleading audiences.
